title: Ordinary Jacobian torsion away from an ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $S$ a finite type commutative $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Assume $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Choose a finite polynomial presentation $\alpha:A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]\twoheadrightarrow S$ with kernel $K$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and let $d_\alpha:K/K^2\to S^{\oplus r}$ be the $S$-linear map $\bar f\mapsto(\partial f/\partial x_i\bmod K)_i$. Then there exists $c\geq0$ such that $I^c\ker d_\alpha=0$ and $I^c\operatorname{coker}d_\alpha=0$, where annihilation means that every element of $I^c$ acts as zero through $A\to S$.

source.place: Tag 0ALQ (lemma-rig-etale), proof of part (1), converse paragraph; the finite-generation and common-power argument uses the finite presentation and Noetherian hypotheses.

proof.text: Put $P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$, $M_1=\ker d_\alpha$ and $M_0=\operatorname{coker}d_\alpha$. Both $P$ and $S$ are finite type over the Noetherian ring $A$, so both are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Thus $K=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ for some finite list, by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Their classes generate $K/K^2$ over $S$: in an expression $f=\sum p_jf_j$, replace $p_j$ by $\alpha(p_j)$, since $K$ acts trivially modulo $K^2$. The standard coordinate vectors generate $S^{\oplus r}$. Hence both terms of $d_\alpha$ are finite $S$-modules, and [lem-pc-noetherian-finite-kernels-cokernels] makes $M_1$ and $M_0$ finite. Fix finite generating lists for both modules as in [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), Tag 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic); restricted.tex Tag 0ALQ (lemma-rig-etale), finiteness paragraph.

proof.text: Fix $a\in I$ and write $g=\alpha(a)\in S$. The principal-open identification [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] identifies $\operatorname{Spec}S_g$ with the inverse image of $D_A(a)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$: contraction of primes tests membership by $a\notin\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\iff g\notin\mathfrak q$. By [lem-a1-etale-open-restriction], the assumed etale restriction induces an etale map to $D_A(a)$. That open immersion into $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale and the composite is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Present $S_g$ over $A$ by $\beta:P[z]\twoheadrightarrow S_g$, $z\mapsto g^{-1}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-naive-cotangent], its kernel is $J=(K,az-1)$, hence finitely generated by Step 1. The conormal differential of $\beta$ is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-conormal-criterion]; this criterion applies to the chosen presentation, not just an existential etale chart. The polynomial differential basis and formula of [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis] identify $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)$ with $(K/K^2\xrightarrow{d_\alpha}S^{\oplus r})$. The principal-localization comparison identifies $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)$ with its localization plus $(S_g\xrightarrow{g}S_g)$. The latter summand is acyclic since $g$ is a unit, so $(d_\alpha)_g$ has zero kernel and cokernel. Localize the short exact sequences $0\to M_1\to K/K^2\to\operatorname{im}d_\alpha\to0$ and $0\to\operatorname{im}d_\alpha\to S^{\oplus r}\to M_0\to0$ using [lem-sc-p1-localization-short-exact]; they identify $(M_1)_g$ and $(M_0)_g$ with those zero modules.

source.place: Tag 0ALQ (lemma-rig-etale), converse paragraph; algebra.tex Tags 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL), 00U1 (definition-etale), 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy), 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), 00HT (lemma-flat-localization); schemes.tex Tag 01I3; morphisms.tex Tags 02GJ, 02GP, 02GN.

proof.text: Choose $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$ by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For every generator $u$ of either finite module from Step 1, Step 2 gives $u/1=0$ in its localization at the image of $a_j$. By the zero-fraction criterion of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], $a_j^{e_{j,u}}u=0$ for some $e_{j,u}\ge0$. Take $e_j\ge1$ at least all these finitely many exponents (take $e_j=1$ for empty lists). By $S$-linearity and [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], $a_j^{e_j}M_1=a_j^{e_j}M_0=0$. If $m=0$, then $I=0$ and $c=1$ works. Otherwise put $c=1+\sum_{j=1}^m(e_j-1)$. Expanding products of $c$ elements of $(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$ shows that $I^c$ is generated by monomials $\prod_j a_j^{v_j}$ with $\sum_jv_j=c$. Such a monomial has some $v_j\ge e_j$, since the opposite inequalities would imply $\sum_jv_j\le\sum_j(e_j-1)=c-1$. It therefore kills both modules. Sums of its $A$-multiples also kill them. Thus $I^cM_1=I^cM_0=0$, where throughout scalars act through $A\to S$, as required.

lean.statement: theorem finite_type_jacobian_torsion_etale_away {A S : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing S] [Algebra A S] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hfinite : (algebraMap A S).FiniteType) (hetale : AlgebraicGeometry.Etale ((Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A S))) ∣_ ⟨(PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A))ᶜ, (PrimeSpectrum.isClosed_zeroLocus (I : Set A)).isOpen_compl⟩)) (r : ℕ) (P : Generators A S (Fin r)) : ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ a ∈ I ^ c, (∀ x : LinearMap.ker (P.cotangentRestrict (u := _root_.id) Function.injective_id), algebraMap A S a • x = 0) ∧ (∀ x : (Fin r →₀ S) ⧸ LinearMap.range (P.cotangentRestrict (u := _root_.id) Function.injective_id), algebraMap A S a • x = 0)
